maya: quick share — ran an AWQ + SmoothQuant variant (we're calling it "smoothfusion") on redwood-13b for very long-context QA (32k and 64k). seeing a consistent bias to earlier parts of the context on answers and some embedding drift. any ideas? :thinking:
kevin: can you paste the small repro + numbers?
maya: summary first: float32 baseline (64k) QA F1 82.1, perplexity 3.9, embed cos 0.984. AWQ+smoothfusion (act-aware enabled) QA F1 76.2 (-5.9), perplexity 4.6, embed cos 0.945. latency +6%. same pattern at 32k but delta smaller (~-3.1 F1).
dani: wow that's a sizable drop. did you change KV cache layout or any layer fusion?
maya: no layout change. same runtime. conversion pipeline:```bash
python tools/convert_quant.py \  --model redwood/13b-fp32 \  --method awq \  --act-aware \  --smoothquant \  --seq 65536 \  --out /tmp/13b_awq_sf.pt
```
kevin: what's the act scale schedule? fixed per-layer or activation-aware per-block?
maya: per-block learned act-scaling (default in our converter).
sam: any token-level loss spikes early in generation? logs?
maya: attached a tiny excerpt from a regen run (compressed):```text
seed=42 prompt_len=2048 gen_len=512
logprobs(start tokens): mean -1.12
logprobs(earlier answer tokens): mean -0.85
logprobs(late answer tokens): mean -1.55
```
maya: so the model strongly prefers earlier context candidates, score-wise.
dani: could be activation clipping from smoothquant quant scales interacting with KV precision. do you see any NaNs or out-of-range activations?
maya: no NaNs. max activation magnitude increased ~14% on a few layers (layer 5/6/20).
kevin: try ablation: AWQ without smoothquant, and smoothquant without act-aware. also try disabling learned act-scale and use static per-layer scale.
maya: already did two quick ablations: AWQ alone -> F1 80.8 (-1.3 vs FP32). SmoothQuant + AWQ without act-aware -> F1 78.9. so act-aware + smoothquant combo is worst.
tony: interesting. could be that act-aware is optimizing for per-timestep norm but biases prefix tokens because scale is learned on shorter contexts. did you train scalers on short ctx only?
maya: conversion used calibration set of 2k token windows sampled from mix of docs (default). maybe that is the mismatch.
sam: try calibrating on longer windows (16k slices) and/or include synthetic prompts that test retrieval from late context.
maya: running a long-window calibration now (job id job_9812).
ops-bot: job_9812 queued on cluster-gpu-2 (ETA ~18m) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
kevin: also check KV quant fallback — runtime may be falling back to FP16 in parts, creating inconsistency between key/value precision. can you grep serving logs for "kv_fallback"?
maya: grep shows a few lines: `kv_fallback: layer6 true, layer20 true (during 64k runs)`
dani: that could explain intermittent scoring differences — mixed-precision path. maybe act-aware scales amplify the mismatch.
kevin: experiments to run (short list):
- calibrate on long windows (16k-64k)
- run AWQ only, SmoothQuant only, AWQ+SmoothQuant with static act-scale, AWQ+SmoothQuant with long-window cal
- enable full fp16 kv path (force) vs mixed path and compare
- small eval: 200 QA pairs with target answers positioned at start vs end of context

maya: updating experiment matrix and will link results. current plan: run 4 calibrations x 3 runtime kv modes x 2 seeds. could be ~24 jobs.
kevin: rough hypothesis: act-aware scalers learned on short contexts + smoothquant redistribution reduce late-context activations below decision threshold -> earlier candidates get relatively higher score.
dani: yep. also check embedding drift metric per position (cosine vs baseline) — if embeddings for late-context drop -> retrieval and similarity-based scoring will break.
maya: noted. initial embedding per-position plot attached (small ascii):```text
pos 0-1024: 0.983
pos 1025-8192: 0.977
pos 8193-32768: 0.945
```
kevin: that makes it obvious.
maya: assigning follow-ups: @kevin to add forced-fp16-kv runtime flag to infra, @dani to try static act-scale conversion, @sam to prepare long-window calibration dataset. i'll run the matrix and post results in this thread.
tony: if this is calibration mismatch, it's a relatively simple fix — either calibrate on long windows or regularize scaler learning to prioritize long-tail activations.
maya: agreed. running now, will drop a short digest when done. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: 👀
dani: :raised_hands:
sam: good plan, ping if you need extra GPUs.
